notes:
I couldn't write these notes because the research didn't work. My one batch of page requests (Enduring Word, Ellicott, Gill and Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub, Precept Austin, and the NET Bible notes) came back in a format my script didn't expect, and it crashed before saving any text. When I tried again to see what had come back, the tool said I'd used up my calls for this turn. I can't reach the web any other way, so I haven't read any of the sources.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for every point. That means I can't write notes from memory, so I haven't included any.

**Next step:** if you ask me to continue in a new message, I'll try again. I'd start by reading the pages listed above, then search the tradition-specific sites for the places Protestant traditions really differ on this psalm. That includes Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* on spurgeon.org, Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, Matthew Henry, Ryle and others on studylight.org and ccel.org, and Lutheran sources. After that I'd check the Catholic and Orthodox sites (Augustine on the Psalms at newadvent.org, plus catholic.com and oca.org) and look for any prosperity or word-of-faith readings of v. 7. Then I'll write the verse-by-verse notes with a URL for each point.
